messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for dedicated-pool:delta in eu-west-1 (SLO window 5m) — p95=780ms p99=2.4s queue_depth=124 streaming-stalls=18. Pager: @oncall-elias
oncall-elias: Acked. I’m on it. Bringing up logs and graphs.
elaine: saw the same in the dashboard, tail-latency spike coincides with a burst at 12:03 UTC. A bunch of warmup handshakes in progress + autoscaler lag.
samir: attaching quick metric snippets: 
```
metric: dedicated-pool:delta.p99 2.4s
metric: request.queue.depth 124
metric: warmup.pending 9
metric: handshake.failures 4
```
ryan: streaming stalls look correlated with `handshake_timeout` errors in the runtime. Logs show repeated `KV_CACHE_COLDPATH` and `HANDSHAKE_RETRY` loops.
maria: any customer impact yet?
cust-success-jordan: we just got an alert from Acme — their integration reported truncated streaming responses and client-side retries. They saw partial responses ~10:03am local, multiple reconnects. They're asking if we have mitigation.
oncall-elias: initial mitigation plan: 1) route traffic off pool:delta to hosted-fallback small model for new sessions; 2) manually provision +2 nodes to pool:delta to drain queue; 3) temporarily lower batch_size and disable long-poll streaming batching. Doing 1 now.
elaine: routing change applied: `route-policy pool:delta -> hosted-fallback` for non-enterprise tenants. Telemetry shows incoming rate drop 40%. Queue depth down to 68 after 90s.
samir: provisioning extra nodes — submitting manual allocation to Dedicated control plane: `POST /admin/pools/delta/scale?count=+2` returned `202 accepted`. Warmup kicked off.
ryan: seeing the autoscaler logs: `scaleup initiated but handshake delay 32s` — autoscaler backoff is aggressive for this workload. That explains the lag.
oncall-elias: while new nodes warm, flip a circuit to avoid batching that increases tail latency: `SET pool.delta.batch.max_tokens=256` -> applied. Monitoring for p95/p99.
maria: pinging CS: Jordan, we routed new incoming streams to hosted fallback and are provisioning extra capacity. Apologize to Acme, will follow up in 30m with update. :phone: 
cust-success-jordan: confirmed — Acme is seeing fewer truncated streams after routing change, but they still have some in-flight retries. They're grateful for the quick mitigation.
elaine: health check logs from new nodes: `warmup.status=loading_kv_cache` — takes ~18-22s per node. We have 2 new nodes at 60% ready.
samir: quick diagnostic: `kubectl logs -n runtime runtime-agent-xyz | grep HANDSHAKE` shows multiple `HANDSHAKE_HELD waiting for kv` and `HANDSHAKE_OK` later. The warmup concurrency default is 1 per node — that's probably the slow path.
oncall-elias: temporary tweak: bump warmup concurrency to 3 for pool:delta via admin API: `PATCH /admin/pools/delta/config {"warmup.concurrency":3}` — applied. 
ryan: after the tweak, handshake completion per node dropped from ~22s -> ~8s. Queue depth now 9. p95 down to 220ms, p99 down to 610ms. Still monitoring for streaming stalls.
maria: customer update sent to Acme w/ summary and ETA for full resolution.
cust-success-jordan: they appreciate the update and asked if we can avoid this in the future — flagged as high for their account.
elaine: root cause notes so far: rapid burst of requests exposed slow warmup handshake on dedicated nodes; autoscaler backoff and conservative warmup concurrency caused delayed capacity; combined with streaming batching created tail latency amplification.
oncall-elias: current status: mitigations in place, traffic partially routed, manual scale and warmup-concurrency bump completed. Observed metrics trending towards SLO. Moving to monitoring->close once stable for 15m.
samir: filed short-lived hotfix to autoscaler backoff for pool:delta: `reduce backoff window to 1s for first 2 attempts` — rolled as feature-flagged change.
ryan: created a quick fallback rule in routing: if queue_depth>50 and pool.warmup.pending>3 then route to hosted-fallback automatically. Feature-flagged and enabled for eu-west-1.
maria: paging follow-up: schedule oncall debrief at 30m, CS to run customer impact spreadsheet, send notice to accounts.
cust-success-jordan: confirmed Acme will wait for the follow-up and asked for postmortem.
oncall-elias: closing loop: mark incident as `mitigated` for immediate paging. Will open postmortem with action items: (1) increase default warmup concurrency for bursty pools, (2) adjust autoscaler backoff heuristics, (3) add routing fallback rule, (4) add a synthetic test for streaming under warmup conditions.
elaine: +1. I'll own the postmortem write-up.
samir: logging ticket to improve warmup telemetry (more granular per-handshake timing).
ryan: leaving monitoring on for next 45m. If p99 creeps back up, re-open page.
oncall-elias: thanks team — great run. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> monitoring (p95/p99 back under alert thresholds). Posted runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-warmup-tail-2026
elaine: follow-ups: quick RFC to adjust warmup defaults + unit tests for handshake concurrency.
maria: will schedule a customer follow-up email and postmortem review with CS + eng in 48 hours.
cust-success-jordan: closing on customer side, Acme says okay for now and will wait for postmortem.
oncall-elias: final note: create a low-latency alert for streaming stalls (threshold p99 > 1s over 5m) and a playbook entry for immediate routing fallback.
elaine: filing that alert now.
ryan: logs + graphs archived under incident-6365008000.
elaine: thread done — moving to incident tracker.
